transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Taylor Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Pinnacle VP Eng), Ethan Brooks (Pinnacle Platform Eng), Noah Kim (Pinnacle Security)

Summary:
Quick SDK integration walkthrough for Pinnacle Retail focusing on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns (API key, env vars, service tokens), and initial POC steps. Covered hosted vs Dedicated, console quickstart, and security concerns (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Agreed to run a POC benchmark and exchange security docs.

Topics:
- SDK install and auth (Python and TypeScript)
- Environment setup and config (env vars, secrets management)
- Quickstart examples: text generation, embeddings, streaming responses
- Console and Optimize features for batching/quantization recommendations
- Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs, routing and latency considerations
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, VPC, data residency

Action Items (captured in metadata too):
- Taylor to send pricing and Dedicated options
- Ravi to share GitHub quickstart and sample snippets
- Pinnacle to confirm data residency and compliance needs

Transcript Body:
00:00 Taylor: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, i think. so quick intros, i'm taylor with redwood, ae, and ravi/se are here to go through the SDKs and a quick quickstart.
00:12 Maya: hi, maya here, vp eng at pinnacle. excited to see how quickly we can get inference into our platform.
00:18 Ethan: ethan, platform eng, i'll be doing the integration work.
00:22 Noah: noah, security, i'll mostly be checking compliance items.
00:26 Taylor: awesome, cool. ravi, do you wanna kick off with the python walkthrough?
00:30 Ravi: yeah sure, so first thing, we have two SDKs, python and typescript. install for python is pip install redwood-inference (note: package name may vary in GA). quick example, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, or use a service token via our console. python snippet: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = c.generate(model='redwood-7b', prompt='summarize sales data...') — and you'll get a streaming or non-streaming response.
00:55 Ethan: quick q, do you recommend env var or mounted secret? we use k8s sealed secrets.
00:59 Ravi: both are fine; for k8s you'd use your secret manager and mount it. we also support direct integration with vaults and kinesis, sorry, k-m-s for key management for Dedicated/private deployments. for hosted, simple env var is common for dev.
01:15 Aisha: for TS it's npm i @redwood/inference and then import RedClient from '@redwood/inference'; const c = new RedClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); c.chat.create({ model: 'chat-1', messages: [...] }) — streaming via eventsource or webhooks is supported.
01:35 Maya: nice. latency-wise what should we expect for a 7b-ish model?
01:39 Ravi: depends on hardware and sequence length. hosted, typical p95 for redwood-7b is mid 100s ms for short prompts, but for sustained throughput consider Dedicated. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can reserve GPU pools. also autoscaling policies.
01:58 Ethan: can we pin model versions? cause we want deterministic behavior for tests.
02:02 Ravi: yeah you can pin model versions in the console or via api, and rollouts support canary and A/B experiments. we can show console after SDK.
02:15 Noah: on security, where are logs stored and who has access? do you have audit logs and SSO?
02:20 Taylor: yes soc2, audit logs, sso/saml support, role-based access control. we can share the security whitepaper. for private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
02:32 Noah: are logits or raw model outputs stored? we need to avoid retention of PII.
02:36 Ravi: by default hosted API doesn't persist request bodies past short-term metrics retention unless you opt-in. for enterprise Dedicated/Private you control retention and logs. we'll share exact retention windows in the security doc.
02:50 Maya: ok good. show us a quick TS example of embeddings — we plan to build semantic search.
02:55 Aisha: sure, TS snippet: const embeddings = await c.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-1', input: ['product description 1', 'product description 2'] }); // returns vector arrays. you can batch inputs. we have guidance in Optimize for batching sizes specific to model and hardware.
03:18 Ethan: what's Optimize?
03:20 Ravi: Optimize is our toolkit that analyzes your workload and suggests batching, cache, and quantization configs. it integrates with the console, shows token-cost breakdowns, and flags quality regressions tied to eval sets.
03:34 Maya: can optimize recommend quantization for lower-cost models?
03:37 Ravi: yep. e.g., suggest 4-bit quant profile for certain open models that maintains quality per your evals. note: quantization tradeoffs exist, we'll show suggested profiles and expected latency/cost deltas.
03:50 Ethan: ok we want a POC with sample traffic — can we run a benchmark against our dataset?
03:54 Ravi: yes we can schedule a benchmark week, you provide sample queries and we'll run hosted and Dedicated comparisons, measure latency/p95, and cost estimates.
04:05 Maya: about auth again — do you support short-lived service tokens for ephemeral containers?
04:09 Aisha: yes support for short-lived tokens, and we have an agent for rotating tokens. you can also integrate with your IDP for SSO; for programmatic access it's api keys or service tokens.
04:20 Ethan: what's the SDK pattern for retries and idempotency?
04:23 Ravi: SDK has built-in retry policies, exponential backoff, and idempotency keys for non-streaming calls. for streaming we recommend client-side handling and reconnect logic.
04:35 Maya: any gotchas for node vs python usage?
04:37 Aisha: mainly dependency management. node supports eventsource streaming; python has async streaming. both support typed responses and function/tool calling patterns. note: our python client name will be stable but sometimes package naming is different in previews.
04:50 Noah: about network isolation — can you support VPC peering or private endpoints?
04:54 Taylor: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and private control plane options for on-prem. we'll include a diagram in the docs.
05:05 Ethan: do you expose metrics/tracing? we use prometheus and jaeger.
05:09 Ravi: yes, we have per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. you can pull metrics to prometheus and integrate with your dashboards.
05:20 Maya: let's walk through the console really fast, if possible.
05:23 Taylor: sure, i'll share my screen — (screen share noises) console shows model catalog, routes, tokens usage. you can create an api key in the console under settings -> API Keys, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY. routes are where you can pin a model and set a fallback chain.
05:45 Aisha: in the console optimize tab you'll see batching suggestions, and a timeline of eval regressions. you can upload test prompt sets to get alerts.
05:58 Ethan: sample quickstart repo?
06:00 Ravi: i'll drop the repo link — gist/repo in chat — includes python quickstart: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx; pip install redwood-inference; python examples/generate.py. for TS: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx; npm i @redwood/inference; node examples/chat.js.
06:20 Maya: can we do streaming response to our websocket service?
06:23 Aisha: yes, via eventsource on node or standard streaming protocol from python; we also support webhook fanout if you prefer server-to-server.
06:32 Ethan: any specifics on rate limits during the POC?
06:35 Taylor: hosted has default rate limits, but for the POC we can provision higher quotas or use Dedicated reserved capacity. we'll note that in the POC plan.
06:45 Maya: what's the cost model — per-token and per-embedding?
06:48 Taylor: yes hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity + lower unit costs. we'll include a sample cost estimate in the pricing doc.
06:58 Noah: last compliance q, do you support data residency in eu?
07:02 Ravi: yes multi-region support, EU regions available. for strict residency you might want Private or Dedicated in-region deployments.
07:12 Maya: great. recap of next steps?
07:15 Taylor: okay recap: we'll send pricing + Dedicated options, security pack (SOC2, KMS notes), and the quickstart repo. we'll schedule POC benchmark run — suggest week of 2026-02-09. ravi will run the benchmark with your sample set. noah will confirm residency and retention needs.
07:35 Ethan: sounds good.
07:37 Noah: thanks all, i'll look for the security docs.
07:40 Taylor: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links and a calendar invite for the POC planning.

End of transcript.

References shared in chat: https://github.com/redwood/inference-quickstarts (quickstart repo), link to security whitepaper (redwood.com/security.pdf), pricing spreadsheet (redwood.com/pricing/pinnacle-estimate.xlsx)
